page: Amazon Web Services r5d.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The system features 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores across an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. Compute features include support for AVX and AVX-512 instructions, AES cryptography, and BMI2 instructions. The platform includes 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Attached storage comprises 2,400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage, supplemented by a baseline network throughput of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong sustained uncached memory bandwidth, reaching 209.41 GB/sec for large block reads and 92.36 GB/sec for writes. In contrast, single-thread compute capabilities remain modest, registering weak scores across Geekbench single-core (1057.0), single-threaded gzip compression (21.96 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (8.47 GB/sec). Multi-core benchmarks place the system in the middle tier, with a PassMark CPU score of 42683.3, a Geekbench multi-core score of 11070.0, and static web serving throughput of 36.14 GB/sec.

The hardware configuration provides high RAM density and local NVMe storage without dedicating resources to GPU acceleration. Because single-thread throughput is lower compared to newer compute-oriented architectures, workload efficiency is highest when parallel processing can exploit the combined 64 vCPUs, deep 35 MB L3 cache, and high-bandwidth RAM. It is particularly fit for in-memory caching solutions like Redis, large-scale relational database engines requiring fast local scratch storage, real-time analytics, and data-intensive ETL pipelines.
